title: Hot Work: MIG Welding and Grinding Safety
status: DRAFT FOR TECHNICAL AND IMS REVIEW

slides.title: Title and training pathway
bullets: This module introduces hot-work controls for MIG welding, grinding and related tasks.
Complete the online checks, then demonstrate the assigned task onsite.
Theory completion alone does not grant task authorisation.

check.question: A worker finishes this online module and is assigned a hot-work task. What must happen before independent work?
options: The online result is enough at any site.
The worker's role, practical competence, site requirements and task authorisation must be verified.
A colleague's verbal assurance replaces the site process.
check.feedback: The online result is theory evidence. A competent assessor and responsible person must complete the required practical and site authorisation steps.

slides.title: Why hot-work control matters
bullets: Arc radiation, fumes, sparks, hot metal, electricity and gas systems can harm workers and bystanders.
Control the work area and equipment before creating an ignition source.
Incorrect WPS selection or lost traceability can also create quality and IMS failures.

check.question: Packaging is beside a weld area and a worker says only the weld quality matters. What is the correct response?
options: Start welding and move the packaging later.
Control the fire exposure and confirm the work and quality requirements before starting.
Ask the next shift to inspect the area.
check.feedback: Hot work must be planned for both safety and quality. Combustibles and the applicable job requirements need attention before work.

slides.title: Learning objectives
bullets: Recognise task hazards and select the relevant risk assessment, permit and site controls.
Inspect PPE, welding equipment, grinders, leads and cylinders.
Stop when conditions change, then complete onsite practical verification.

check.question: A trade assistant can list the hazards but has not demonstrated the assigned weld. What is still needed?
options: Nothing; naming the hazards proves competence.
Onsite demonstration and the required role and supervisor authorisation.
Only a higher online quiz score.
check.feedback: Knowing the hazards is one part of competence; the assigned work must be demonstrated and authorised.

slides.title: What counts as hot work?
bullets: Welding, grinding and thermal cutting can create ignition sources, fumes, heat or flying particles.
Consider the actual task and surroundings, even for a short tack or clean-up grind.
Apply the site hot-work process when the task can expose people or ignite material.

check.question: A quick angle-grinder clean-up will create sparks near stored packaging. How should it be treated?
options: As routine housekeeping with no hot-work controls.
As spark-producing work requiring assessment and the applicable area and fire controls.
As hot work only if a welding arc is used.
check.feedback: Grinding can be hot work when it creates sparks or an ignition risk.

slides.title: IMS requirements for hot work
bullets: Use the current approved task documents and record the applicable worker briefing or sign-on.
Confirm induction, task competence, site conditions and consultation.
File permits, inspections, training and nonconformance records in the approved IMS process.
slides.verify: Insert the current Panalo Pipes document IDs, revision controls, records and role-specific competence requirements before controlled issue. A SWMS is legally required for Victorian high-risk construction work; other tasks still need their applicable risk controls.

check.question: A job pack contains a superseded task assessment. What should the crew do?
options: Use it because the task looks familiar.
Hold the work and obtain the current approved documents, then brief workers on the actual controls.
Sign the old version and replace it after the shift.
check.feedback: Document control and worker communication are part of the IMS control, not after-work paperwork.

slides.title: Hot-work permit and authorisation
bullets: Define the scope and work area, control combustibles, and confirm fire, fume, PPE and equipment controls.
Complete and review the host permit and applicable SWMS or task assessment before work where required.
The responsible person authorises the start and confirms monitoring and close-out arrangements.
slides.verify: The visual shows a 10 m combustible clearance and a 30-minute fire watch. These figures are illustrative and must be checked against the approved site permit, risk assessment and applicable standard before use. Confirm who issues, signs, monitors and closes the permit.

check.question: The area is prepared, but the host site's required hot-work permit has not been authorised. What happens?
options: Begin while the supervisor completes the permit.
Do not start; obtain the required permit and authorisation after the controls are verified.
Start only the first tack weld.
check.feedback: Where a permit is required, work starts only after its controls and authorisation are in place.

slides.title: SWMS and JSA control focus
bullets: The task document should identify work steps, hazards, controls and how they will be checked.
For Victorian high-risk construction work, use an applicable SWMS that covers the actual activity and controls.
When location, scope or conditions change, stop and review the assessment and permit as required.
slides.verify: Confirm HRCW screening, the approved Panalo Pipes procedure and JSA IDs, and the host SWMS and permit requirements for the assigned job.

check.question: A site weld moves beside another trade and the approved controls no longer fit. What is required?
options: Keep the original sign-on and proceed.
Pause, make safe, reassess with the responsible person and update the applicable documents and controls before authorised restart.
Ask the other trade to move without changing the work plan.
check.feedback: A changed work area can change fire, fume, access and exclusion controls.

slides.title: Hazard hotspot review
bullets: Find arc radiation, welding fumes, sparks, hot metal and damaged electrical leads.
Check grinder setup, cylinders, combustible waste and the exclusion zone.
Look beyond the picture for coatings, nearby work and site-specific ignition paths.

check.question: Sparks can reach a bin of oily rags shown in the hotspot. What should be done before welding?
options: Remove or protect the combustibles and verify the spark path and fire arrangements.
Turn down the welding current and leave the rags.
Warn the next shift once work is finished.
check.feedback: Control combustible material and check the fire arrangements before producing sparks.

slides.title: Welding fumes and ventilation
bullets: Use effective source capture or other assessed engineering controls where practicable.
Keep the breathing zone out of the fume plume and check whether extraction remains effective.
Respiratory protection may be needed under the task assessment, but it does not replace practicable higher controls.

check.question: The required extraction hood has stopped working. What should the welder do?
options: Weld quickly with a mask and a door open.
Stop, make safe and have the responsible person restore or approve effective fume controls before restart.
Stand closer to the plume to check its direction.
check.feedback: A failed required control calls for reassessment; PPE alone is not an automatic substitute for source control.

slides.title: Hot-work PPE
bullets: Inspect the welding helmet and lens, eye and face protection, hearing protection, FR clothing, gloves and boots.
Choose respiratory protection and high-visibility elements according to the task assessment and site rules.
Fit and maintain PPE correctly while keeping engineering and area controls in place.
slides.verify: Confirm mandatory and conditional PPE for each role, process and client site against the current approved procedure, SDS and assessment. The visual is a draft example.

check.question: A respirator is available but source extraction required by the task assessment is absent. What is the safe decision?
options: Use the respirator as the only control and proceed.
Do not start until the control arrangement is reviewed and approved; select PPE as part of that assessment.
Ask a bystander to hold the hood by hand.
check.feedback: PPE selection does not remove the need to address the missing required fume control.

slides.title: Grinding: correct and unsafe practice
bullets: Use the manufacturer-specified tool and disc with its guard and handle fitted.
Check the disc condition, secure the workpiece and control sparks and nearby people.
Do not use a damaged disc, remove the guard or fit an unsuitable blade.

check.question: A grinder's guard is missing, but the disc looks sound. What should the worker do?
options: Work carefully without the guard.
Keep the grinder out of service until the correct guard and disc setup are restored and checked.
Wear thicker gloves and proceed.
check.feedback: A sound disc does not address a missing guard. Make the tool safe and report the defect.

slides.title: Gas cylinder storage and use
bullets: Keep cylinders identified, upright and secured; protect valves during storage and movement.
Inspect regulators and hoses and keep cylinders clear of heat and spark exposure.
Isolate and report suspected leaks or damage under the site procedure.
slides.verify: Confirm the gas type, storage and segregation arrangements and any separation distances with the approved gas procedure, SDS and site requirements. The picture includes oxy-fuel cylinders as a broader hot-work example.

check.question: A hose is damaged and a cylinder is unsecured near hot work. What is the next action?
options: Continue only with a fire extinguisher nearby.
Stop, make safe, report the defects and restore the approved cylinder and hose setup before work.
Move the cylinder closer so the hose is less stretched.
check.feedback: A damaged gas system or unsecured cylinder is a stop-work condition.

slides.title: Fire prevention and fire watch
bullets: Remove or protect combustibles and consider where sparks can travel, including hidden spaces.
Confirm suitable extinguishing equipment, access and a fire watch when required by the permit and assessment.
Continue post-work checks and close out the permit according to site requirements.
slides.verify: Set the fire-watch assignment, duration and close-out criteria in the approved site permit. Do not apply the visual's example timing as a universal rule.

check.question: The welding has ended, but the required fire-watch period and area check are not complete. What should happen?
options: Leave because no flame is visible.
Maintain the assigned watch and checks under the permit until the responsible person confirms close-out.
Remove the extinguisher and ask the next shift to look later.
check.feedback: Hot metal and hidden smouldering material can remain after the arc stops; use the approved post-work arrangements.

slides.title: Exclusion zones and nearby workers
bullets: Use screens and barriers to protect others from arc radiation, sparks and flying particles.
Communicate with adjacent trades and keep hoses, leads and offcuts controlled.
Stop if the agreed exclusion zone cannot be maintained.

check.question: Another worker enters the spark path while grinding. What should the operator do?
options: Continue because that worker has safety glasses.
Stop the task and restore the exclusion controls before resuming.
Only turn the grinder away without speaking to the worker.
check.feedback: The work area must protect nearby people as well as the operator.

slides.title: Equipment pre-start inspection
bullets: Check leads, torch, return clamp, grinder guard, handle and correct disc.
Check cylinder security, hoses, regulator, fire gear and area readiness.
Remove defective equipment from service and report it before energising.

check.question: The pre-start finds a cracked grinder disc. What should the worker do?
options: Use the good-looking side for one quick pass.
Do not use it; make the tool safe, report the defect and replace the disc through the approved process.
Fit a face shield and continue.
check.feedback: A cracked disc is a stop-work defect; PPE cannot make it safe.

slides.title: Safe work sequence
bullets: Plan the scope and documents; prepare the area and controls; inspect tools and PPE.
Monitor sparks, fumes, people and changing conditions throughout the task.
Close out by shutting down, managing hot metal, checking for fire and completing required records.

check.question: The weld is complete and the machine is off. Which sequence step remains?
options: Leave immediately because the arc is off.
Manage hot metal, inspect for smouldering material, restore the area and complete required handover or records.
Move the fire gear away before checking the area.
check.feedback: Close-out is part of the safe work sequence.

slides.title: Stop work and change management
bullets: Stop and make safe when a critical control is missing, failed or uncertain.
Notify the responsible person and reassess the actual task and conditions.
Update the relevant assessment and permit, then obtain required restart authorisation.

check.question: A client changes the work location and the extraction cannot reach it. What is the next step?
options: Start with a respirator while a colleague watches.
Stop, make safe, notify, reassess the new area and controls, then seek required approval before restart.
Complete the tack welds first because they are short.
check.feedback: A change in location and failed extraction require a new approved control arrangement.

slides.title: Emergency and incident response
bullets: Raise the alarm and follow the site's emergency plan.
Make safe or use fire equipment only when trained and safe; arrange first aid and evacuation as directed.
Notify the supervisor and complete the required incident or near-miss report.
slides.verify: Insert verified emergency contacts, evacuation route, muster point and client reporting instructions before formal issue.

check.question: Smoke is noticed beside the hot-work area during a break. What should the worker do first?
options: Raise the alarm and follow the site emergency arrangements, making safe only if safe.
Wait for the fire watch before telling anyone.
Resume welding to locate the smoke source.
check.feedback: Prompt alarm and the site emergency response take priority.

slides.title: Quality and IMS controls
bullets: Confirm the current drawing, applicable WPS, welder qualification and material identification before production welding.
Maintain weld and material traceability and observe assigned inspection hold points.
Record NDT requests and nonconformances where the job requires them.
slides.verify: Insert the exact approved WPS, WPQ, ITP, MTC, NDT and NCR document IDs and revisions for the assigned scope.

check.question: The job pack has a WPS for a different joint and the material heat number is unclear. What should happen?
options: Choose the nearest WPS and reconstruct the heat number later.
Hold the weld and obtain the correct approved WPS and traceability instructions.
Weld first and ask quality staff to repair the record.
check.feedback: Wrong procedure or missing traceability needs resolution before production welding.

slides.title: Five critical rules and final theory assessment
bullets: Use the applicable current task documents and permit before work.
Control fumes, fire, sparks, hot metal and nearby people; inspect equipment and cylinders.
Stop when conditions are unsafe or changed. Complete the final theory assessment below, followed by onsite practical verification.

exam.question: Before starting assigned hot work, what should be confirmed?
options: Only that the welder powers on.
Scope, worker authorisation, current documents, site permit where required and area controls.
That another crew worked there yesterday.

exam.question: A host permit is required but not authorised. What should happen?
options: Begin only a short tack.
Do not start until the permit and its controls are verified and authorised.
Start while the form is completed.

exam.question: When is a SWMS legally required for Victorian construction work?
options: For every workshop weld.
For high-risk construction work as defined by the Victorian OHS Regulations.
Only after an incident.

exam.question: Sparks can reach combustible packaging. What is the correct action?
options: Remove or protect it and check the spark path and fire arrangements.
Weld at a lower current without changing the area.
Ask the next shift to inspect it.

exam.question: The required fume extraction stops. What is the safe response?
options: Weld quickly with a mask.
Stop and have an effective approved fume-control arrangement restored or reassessed.
Stand closer to see the plume.

exam.question: Which action protects nearby workers from arc radiation and grinding particles?
options: Ask them to look away.
Use assessed screens, barriers and exclusion controls.
Assume the operator's PPE protects them.

exam.question: A grinder guard is missing and the disc has a crack. What should the worker do?
options: Use it carefully for one pass.
Remove it from service, report and restore the correct guard and disc setup.
Add heavier gloves.

exam.question: A gas hose is damaged near a cylinder. What is needed?
options: Continue if the extinguisher is close.
Make safe, report the defect and restore the approved gas setup.
Tape the hose for the remaining weld.

exam.question: The work location changes beside another trade. What should happen before restart?
options: Use the original controls unchanged.
Reassess the area and update applicable documents, permit and controls with required authorisation.
Ask the other trade to watch the sparks.

exam.question: A required fire watch is still in progress after welding. What should the crew do?
options: Maintain the watch and close-out checks under the approved site permit.
Leave once the arc is off.
Remove the extinguisher to tidy the area.

exam.question: What belongs in an equipment pre-start?
options: Inspect leads, torch, grinder guard and disc, cylinder security and fire controls.
Check only the machine paint and power switch.
Inspect after the shift instead.

exam.question: Smoke is detected during a hot-work break. What is the first response?
options: Raise the alarm and follow the site emergency plan; make safe only if safe.
Wait to see if it clears.
Restart welding to identify the source.

exam.question: The WPS does not match the assigned joint. What should the welder do?
options: Choose a similar WPS from memory.
Hold the weld and obtain the current approved applicable WPS.
Weld and correct the paperwork later.

exam.question: A worker passes online theory. Can they perform the task independently?
options: Yes, the score is enough.
Only after the required onsite practical verification and task authorisation.
Yes, if a colleague is nearby.

exam.question: Before leaving the completed hot-work area, what remains?
options: Nothing after the machine is off.
Manage hot metal, complete the area and fire checks and close out records under site requirements.
Only sign the time sheet.
